extracted.intended_audience: education researchers, program evaluators, district/state writing assessment coordinators, and teachers implementing the 6+1 Trait Writing model
extracted.subtask_description: Rubric and implementation standards for scoring student writing and for delivering the 6+1 Trait Writing professional development and classroom practices (grade-5 context). Includes scoring protocols, trait-specific rubrics, teacher-survey measures, fidelity thresholds, and recommended instructional cycles and strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Holistic writing score (holistic scale)
rubrics_metrics.description: A single holistic score assigned to each student essay representing overall writing performance, used as the primary outcome for impact analyses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Holistic scores were positively correlated with the six trait scales (Pearson r range 0.49–0.66 across pretest/posttest). Combined, the six trait scales accounted for 75.2% of variance in the holistic scale at pretest and 80.6% at posttest. The holistic scale was used in the main multilevel impact model as the outcome variable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trait-specific rubrics (six core traits)
rubrics_metrics.description: Six separate rubrics—one for each of six core traits in the 6+1 Trait Writing model—were used to rate essays as additional outcome measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The six trait scales were scored in addition to the holistic score to provide trait-level sensitivity to program effects; trait-specific scores were used for exploratory analyses. The trait of presentation was not scored on the assessment because the test required a standard presentation format. When analyzing trait scores, the six were treated as theoretically independent and no multiple-comparisons adjustment was applied to the six exploratory tests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ideas (trait)
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the six core trait rubrics used to evaluate student essays (ideas).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Introduced in teacher training and emphasized in instruction (one of two traits emphasized during first three months). Trait scores were positively correlated with the holistic score and were used as outcome variables in exploratory analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organization (trait)
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the six core trait rubrics used to evaluate student essays (organization).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasized along with ideas during the first three months of instruction; used as a trait-specific outcome in exploratory analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Word choice (trait)
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the six core trait rubrics used to evaluate student essays (word choice).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Introduced at the summer institute and emphasized during a follow-up workshop (first one-day workshop emphasized word choice and conventions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sentence fluency (trait)
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the six core trait rubrics used to evaluate student essays (sentence fluency).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Introduced and emphasized during training (second workshop focused on sentence fluency and conventions) and used for trait-level analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voice (trait)
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the six core trait rubrics used to evaluate student essays (voice).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Introduced and emphasized during training (third workshop focused on voice, presentation, and conventions); used for trait-level analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conventions (trait)
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the six core trait rubrics used to evaluate student essays (conventions: capitalization, punctuation, spelling, grammar).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conventions were emphasized throughout the year (at the summer institute and each subsequent workshop) because developers recommend spreading conventions instruction across the entire school year rather than short, intensive coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rating scale and rater scoring procedure (1–6 scale, averaging, flagging rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each essay was independently scored by two raters using a 1–6 scale; the final essay score was the average of the two raters, reported in half-point increments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scale anchors: 1 indicates a severely flawed essay demonstrating very little or no mastery; 6 indicates an essay demonstrating clear and consistent mastery. If the two raters' scores were identical or one point apart, no further action was taken. If scores exceeded a one-point difference, the essay was flagged and scored by the team leader, who then had the original raters reread and revise their scores in consultation with the leader. This process served both quality assurance and rater training/improvement. Details on interrater reliability are provided in appendix G.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling unscorable essays (language/length rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for essays that could not be scored due to language or minimal length.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Essays not in English and essays of two sentences or less were coded as 'unable to rate' and assigned the lowest possible score during the analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teacher survey measurement method (10 scales)
rubrics_metrics.description: Teacher survey comprised 10 scales corresponding to the 10 classroom practices emphasized by the intervention; each scale contained 3–7 items.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Teachers rated each item on a seven-point scale (0 = 'not emphasized at all' to 6 = 'emphasized very often and strongly'). Scale scores were computed as the mean of items within each scale for each teacher. At initial administration, internal consistency (coefficient alpha) for the scales ranged from 0.78 to 0.92. The full instrument is reproduced in appendix D.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fidelity of implementation classification (nonimplementer/basic/advanced)
rubrics_metrics.description: Study-specific thresholds to classify teachers' fidelity to the 6+1 Trait Writing model based on teacher survey scale scores.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advanced fidelity: teachers who scored above the midpoint (3.0 on the 0–6 scale) on all 10 scales OR scored higher than 4.0 on six or more scales. Basic fidelity: teachers who scored above the midpoint (3.0) on six or more scales but did not meet advanced criteria. Nonimplementers: teachers who did not reach the basic level. These criteria were created for the study based on developer recommendations; their validity relative to observational measures has not been formally established.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instructional cycle for teaching a trait (recommended sequence)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommended cycle of instruction to introduce and teach a particular trait to students.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cycle steps: using the rubric to plan; teaching the language by rewriting the rubric in student-friendly language; scoring papers, justifying scores, and discussing the scoring process; modeling several trait-based activities or focus lessons; creating a writing prompt; gathering a written product for assessment purposes; measuring overall student improvement as well as improvement in the specific trait. Teachers were asked to use this cycle throughout the year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasis schedule for traits over the year
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on which traits to emphasize when during the first year of instruction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All traits introduced at the summer institute; teachers were encouraged to emphasize ideas and organization over the first three months. Conventions were emphasized continually throughout the year and at each workshop. Subsequent workshops emphasized particular traits: first one-day workshop—word choice and conventions; second—sentence fluency and conventions; third—voice, presentation, and conventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teaching the language of rubrics for writing assessment (instructional strategy #1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicit instruction in rubric language so teachers and students understand assessment criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One of the ten trait-based classroom writing instruction strategies introduced in the summer institute and included as a teacher-survey scale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reading and scoring papers, and having students justify scores (instructional strategy #2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Practice of reading and scoring papers, justifying the assigned scores, and involving students in the scoring process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used both as a modeled activity in training and as a survey-measured classroom practice to be implemented regularly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teaching focused revision strategies (instructional strategy #3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Instruction that targets specific revision skills and strategies for improving student writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Modeled during training and measured on the teacher survey as a distinct instructional practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modeling participation in the writing process (instructional strategy #4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Teacher demonstration and modeling of authentic engagement in the writing process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Included in the set of ten strategies and emphasized during professional development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Having students read and analyze materials that demonstrate varying writing quality (instructional strategy #5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of mentor texts and exemplars to show differing levels of writing quality and to guide student analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hundreds of picture books and sample papers were provided during the summer institute for this purpose; teachers practiced analyzing and using such materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Giving writing assignments with effective prompts (instructional strategy #6)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assigning writing tasks that engage students and provide adequate structure, guidance, and context to elicit detailed responses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training included methods for creating prompts; teachers practiced generating their own prompts. The survey measured teachers' use of effective prompts as one of the strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Weaving writing lessons into other subjects (instructional strategy #7)
rubrics_metrics.description: Integrating writing instruction across subject areas rather than isolating it in standalone lessons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presented as a strategy during the summer institute and included in the teacher survey.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teaching students to set goals and monitor their progress (instructional strategy #8)
rubrics_metrics.description: Instruction that helps students establish writing goals and track their improvement over time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Modeled in training and measured on the teacher survey as a distinct practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrating learning goals for writing into curriculum planning (instructional strategy #9)
rubrics_metrics.description: Including explicit writing learning goals when planning broader curriculum units.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treated as one of the ten classroom strategies and assessed via teacher self-report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teaching ways to structure nonfiction writing (instructional strategy #10)
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicit instruction on organization and structure specific to nonfiction genres.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provided as a modeled strategy with supporting materials and included in the teacher survey.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional development delivery format (training protocol)
rubrics_metrics.description: Required format and supports for teacher professional development associated with the intervention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Teachers attended a three-day summer institute (comprehensive training, planning time, and materials) and three additional one-day workshops during the school year. Supports included online resources, sample student papers, scoring practice with expert comparisons, suggested readings, and access to trainers by email/phone. Attendance and participation in these sessions were used to document implementation exposure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of sample papers and rater calibration in training
rubrics_metrics.description: Practices for training teachers and raters to score reliably.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training included scoring student papers, comparing teacher scores to expert raters, and practice activities to align understanding of trait rubrics; these activities were part of the professional development and scoring quality procedures.
